findings:
FINDING F1 — a new writing-rule breach entered the tree in the change that exists to remove writing-rule breaches. Substantiated; blocking.

/home/user/fleet/emitter/tests/src/core/helpers.test.ts:22
`		// The control: the inherited key is reachable, so a walk that included it would see it.`

What is wrong: `.claude/rules/writing.md` § Voice and actor states "Give software no human faculties. A component reports, returns, detects, or refuses; it never knows, thinks, wants, or sees." The comment gives the enumeration ("a walk") the faculty the rule names explicitly.

Why it matters: this is the only such hit in the package — my sweep for `\b(sees|see it|knows|thinks|wants|believes|decides)\b` over README.md, guides/emitter.md, guides/README.md, src/**/*.ts, tests/src/**/*.ts, tests/guides.test.ts, tests/setup.ts, and vite.config.ts returns that line alone. It is prose this unit authored, and it is the same class of defect the round is closing elsewhere: emitter-subj-9 struck the package's only `we` from a `//` comment in a test file under this same rule section, and the refuter confirmed that ruling, so § Voice and actor demonstrably binds test-file line comments in this round's own precedent. Shipping a fresh breach of the section the round is enforcing leaves the package no cleaner on that rule than it started.

What right looks like: replace the line with
`		// The control: the inherited key is reachable, so a walk that included it would collect it.`
`collect` is the function's own verb (`collected` at src/core/helpers.ts:25). `return it` also closes it. Change nothing else in the file; the assertions and the control are correct as they stand.

REFERRALS — to the Orchestrator, no verdict from me.

R1 (carried unchanged from round 1). guides/emitter.md:29-31 still carries value claims no case executes — `clock.emit('tick', Date.now()) // synchronous — every `tick` listener runs now` and `clock.destroy() // teardown — drops every listener, flips `destroyed``. The Manage-listeners fence is now executed, and the refuter scoped emitter-obj-3 to that fence alone, so widening it here would widen the unit. Whether the Surface fence gets its own transcription is a successor-brief decision, not this round's.

R2. The vendoring obligation is real and I confirmed its population independently: `scsr precursor` over `**/guides/emitter.md` under /home/user/fleet returns the mirror in agent, brief, browser, console, database, form, interpret, lsp, mcp, pool, probe, process, program, qualifier, queue, rater, reason, relation, router, sea, server, table, template, terminal, websocket, worker, workflow, and workspace — exactly the checkouts the report's § Shared-file patches names, and no other. Every one of those still carries the pre-change copy. The refresh is a byte copy of emitter's tip, per `.claude/rules/documentation.md` § Parity ("Refresh a mirror rather than rewriting it"), and it must ride the publish wave rather than this unit.

R3. The evidence diff at /home/user/work/evidence/conform-emitter.diff was transcribed with the `Write` tool rather than redirected, as deviation 4 records. It did not mislead me — I read every changed file in the tree and each hunk matches — but regenerate it with `git -C /home/user/fleet/emitter diff HEAD` before it is retained, so the archived artifact is byte-exact.

R4. Deviation 3 stands open for the landing: `git add -N .` moved the `tests/setup.test.ts` removal into the index, so the status reads `D  tests/setup.test.ts` rather than ` D`. The working tree is correct and the writer correctly refused to run a discarding git command to undo it. The Orchestrator's commit covers the same paths either way; decide it at landing rather than sending it back.

CLAIMS ATTACKED AND HELD. I attacked claim 2 by re-reading every prescribed site against the tree rather than against the report, and it held at every one. I attacked claim 3 by re-running every sweep myself over a superset population, unbounded and case-insensitive, and it held. I attacked claim 6 by running the fleet-wide `extractKeys` sweep myself, and it held. I attacked claim 7 by checking the scaffold host inventory to see whether tests/guides.test.ts is a vendored file the unit had no right to edit — it is not. I attacked the type-safety of the emitter-obj-4 repair against the installed `@orkestrel/test` declaration, and the emitter-obj-7 repair against Emitter's snapshot and wrapper-removal path; both hold. I attacked the now export-free tests/setup.ts for the isolatedModules global-script trap, and tsconfig.json:9 `moduleDetection: force` closes it. Nothing in the tree is functionally wrong. The round fails on F1 alone, which is one Edit.
